sentences.text:
Advocate for the Petitioner : Mr. R Ali
Advocate for the Respondent : Ga, Assam
 Before
 Honourable Mr. Justice Manish Choudhury
 Order
Date : 02.06.2023
There is no representation on behalf of the petitioner today on call.

Mr. R. Boro,
learned counsel representing Mr. C. Baruah, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent nos. 1, 2 & 3; Ms. N. Bordoloi, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue Department for the respondent no. 4; and Mr. B. Deuri, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 5 & 6 are present.

From a notice bearing no. GRQ-5/2010-20/Pt-I dated 13.04.2022 [Annexure-4 to the writ petition],
it transpires that the petitioner and one Sri Kamakhya Prasad Rabha were given notices by the said authority to appear before him on 28.04.2021.

It was indicated therein that the noticees were required to submit their supporting documents before him as an amount of compensation had been assessed under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 vide Land Acquisition Case no.
1/2019-2020.
From the said notice as well as from paragraph 5 of the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent no. 5, it is found that an amount of Rs. 3,77,129/- had been assessed towards compensation for zirat.
The two claimants i.e. the petitioner and Sri Kamakhya Prasad Rabha refused to share the compensation.

The plot of land in respect of which such compensation for zirat was assessed, was a Government Khas Land and the claimant, Sri Kamahya Prasad Rabha was paying Bedakhali Jarimona [Encroachment Penalty] for the said land.

Highlighting the above aspects, the learned counsel for the respondents have submitted that the remedy for the petitioner lies in the provisions of Section 3G and Section 3H of the National Highways Act, 1956.
As there is no representation on behalf of the petitioners today on call, list the case on 12.06.2023.
